title: Engine Oil Filter Housing — Drain

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Draining of the engine oil filter housing before a filter element change, with the bayonet hose method used on post modification aircraft and the spillage control required on the delivered arrangement.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to drain the oil filter housing before the filter element is changed or before the housing is removed.
sections.job_setup_note: Hot oil causes burns. Let the engine cool for at least thirty minutes after shutdown, and wear the gloves and eye protection. The method differs by aircraft standard: with the bayonet fitting the hose is attached before the housing is opened and there is no spillage, while on the delivered arrangement the shroud must be lined and the fairing protected because residual oil runs down it.
sections.procedure: 1. Let the engine cool for at least thirty minutes after shutdown. 2. WARNING: OIL IN THE HOUSING IS HOT AND UNDER RESIDUAL PRESSURE. WEAR GLOVES AND EYE PROTECTION. 3. Open the fan cowl and support it on the stay. 4. Position the collection container below the housing. 5. On aircraft post MOD-168240, connect the drain hose to the bayonet fitting and open the drain. 6. On aircraft with the delivered arrangement, line the shroud with the absorbent sheet and protect the pylon lower fairing before the drain is opened. 7. CAUTION: DO NOT ALLOW OIL ONTO THE PYLON LOWER FAIRING. THE STAIN MASKS THE LEAK CHECK AFTER THE NEXT ENGINE RUN. 8. Drain the housing until flow stops and record the quantity recovered. 9. Close the drain and disconnect the hose, or remove the absorbent sheet. 10. Clean any oil from the surrounding structure with the approved agent. 11. Account for the oil recovered against the expected quantity in the table; a low quantity indicates the housing was already partly empty and should be investigated before the element is changed.
sections.close_out: Leave the collection container in position until the filter element change is complete. Wipe the fairing so that the next leak check starts from a clean reference. Record the quantity recovered and any oil condition observation in the aircraft technical log.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; step 5 applies to aircraft post MOD-168240, step 6 to all others

safety_precautions: Let the engine cool for at least thirty minutes after shutdown.
Wear gloves and eye protection when the drain is opened.
